subject: Invoice logs & deletion policy — clarifying what stays for billing
messages:
From: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@acme.com, security@acme.com
Date: 2025-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on deletion requests vs invoice retention

Hi Karthik,

Quick follow-up after our call — finance has a hard requirement to keep invoices and supporting usage logs for seven years for audit. At the same time, our data protection team insists that when an end-customer requests deletion of their data (prompts & model outputs), that data must be removed from all systems. Can you confirm the practical separation between: (A) records we need to keep for billing/audit (invoices, aggregated usage, ledger entries) and (B) customer content that Redwood would delete on request?

Also, is there any case where an invoice or the raw usage detail would be considered "customer content" that must be purged? We've flagged this as a blocker for procurement.

Thanks — John
John Lee
Head of Procurement
Acme Corporation

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on deletion requests vs invoice retention

Hi John — thanks for raising this. Short answer up front: invoices and billing ledgers are financial records and are retained per our finance retention policy; we do not delete invoices when a customer requests deletion of "customer content". I'll outline specifics below and loop in Finance and Security for the edge cases.

Key points:
- Invoice & ledger records: retained for statutory and audit purposes. In the US we retain invoices and the associated billing ledger for 7 years (region-specific retention may vary; we can map for EU/DE specific rules).
- Usage records used for invoicing: we keep the quantitative usage metrics (timestamps, token counts, charge amounts) tied to an invoice in our billing datastore. These are considered financial metadata and are retained to support refunds, chargebacks, and audits.
- Customer content (prompts, responses, documents): treated separately. Per our standard deletion process we remove prompt/response text, files, and KV stores upon a validated deletion request, subject to the exceptions below.

Exceptions / edge cases:
- If customer content is embedded in an invoice PDF (e.g., customer attached a chat transcript as supporting documentation), that supporting file is treated as an attachment and subject to deletion if the customer requests it; however the invoice stub (amount, date, invoice id) remains as a retained financial record.
- Legal holds / compliance: if there's an active legal hold or an audit request, we cannot purge related records until the hold is released. We surface holds to customers during deletion processing.
- Aggregated/derivative usage: aggregated metrics (e.g., daily total tokens for billing buckets) are retained in anonymized form for analytics; these do not contain PII and are not considered customer content.

I'll bring Laura (Finance) into the thread to confirm the finance-side retention language for the contract and Monica to capture any procurement ask.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on deletion requests vs invoice retention

Hi John,

Laura from Finance here. Confirming Redwood's baseline practice:

1) Invoices and billing ledger entries (invoice id, date, line items, totals) are retained for 7 years for US customers to satisfy GAAP and tax audit requirements. We provide copies of invoices on request.

2) Detailed usage exports that include raw prompts or attached customer files are not part of the retained invoice record by default. Our billing exports capture quantitative usage (token counts, model id, request timestamp) but do not store the full prompt/response text in the billing ledger.

3) If Acme requires additional logging for internal reconciliation, we can scope a custom export/retention arrangement in the contract (e.g., store raw request logs in a customer-controlled S3 with agreed retention). That would be a separate commercial/legal conversation.

If you need specific contract language, Monica, can you please propose a clause that clarifies: "Invoices and billing metadata are retained for financial compliance and are excluded from deletion requests targeting customer content."

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2025-11-04T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on deletion requests vs invoice retention

John — looping Legal (Grace) and Sales Ops. Draft clause to propose in SOW/Contract: 

"Billing records and accounting metadata (including invoice identifiers, transaction timestamps, usage metrics used to generate charges, and related payment records) are retained by Redwood Inference for the duration required by applicable financial regulations and are excluded from customer-initiated content deletion requests. Attachments or supporting documents that contain customer-provided content (e.g., chat transcripts uploaded as evidence) will be removed if the customer submits a valid deletion request, subject to applicable legal holds."

Please confirm if that aligns with Acme's procurement needs. If you want a shorter SLA-friendly line for the main MSA, we can make a one-sentence carve-out and push the details to the Privacy Addendum.

Cheers,

Hi all — Grace, Redwood Legal. A couple of points from the legal/compliance side:

- Region specifics: For EU data subjects, deletion requests under GDPR apply to personal data. Billing metadata that contains PII (e.g., billing contact email) may be subject to GDPR; however, Article 6 lawful bases for processing (contract, legal obligation) allow retention of financial records. We recommend a contract clause that references compliance with applicable data protection laws while preserving necessary financial records for statutory obligations.

- Practical approach: We propose two contract exhibits: (1) Privacy Addendum describing deletion process and exceptions; (2) Billing & Audit Addendum that explicitly states retention windows and what constitutes "billing metadata" vs "customer content."

- Edge-case handling: If a customer asks to delete all records and they include specific invoice attachments (e.g., uploaded chat transcript), we will: (a) delete the transcript, (b) maintain the invoice stub, and (c) annotate the invoice record with a note that supporting documentation was removed per deletion request (so audit trail remains intact).

Happy to provide redline language. If Acme wants additional guarantees (e.g., a separate escrowed ledger or customer-managed export of raw logs), that can be commercialized.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
